items.title: A colourful tower
items.description: Start with 28 blocks, then make it your own.
items.prompt: Create a tower with seven layers of four cubes. Use cyan, pink and yellow. Frame the whole tower and slowly orbit around it.

items.title: A burst of colour
items.description: Launch, freeze the action, orbit and let it tumble.
items.prompt: Create a colourful block explosion with a dramatic cinematic style.

steps: Open Scene options (⋯), then Scene settings. The downloaded scene contains 17 controls and five presets.

Start with Breach. On the latest viewer, dust, render quality, chain visibility, masses and friction update live. Launch angle/speed and wall structure stay pending: Apply resets paused, Apply & Play / Replay starts the new setup, and Discard cancels only pending setup edits.
Compare Gentle and Demolition. Keep the same camera and watch how mass and impact speed change the opening and the scattered bricks.
Enable impact dust. Try amount 0.85, cloud size 0.28 m, lifetime 2.4 s, opacity 0.65 and minimum impact energy 1 J.
Choose Mobile for 18 wall rows, lighter shading/LOD and a smaller dust budget. Compare it with Cinematic; do not enable motion blur for the mobile test.
On a recent viewer, hold a brick or the ball while the film plays, then drag and release. The hold wheel is larger and offset on touch screens.
Use the camera toggle to explore freely. Pause leaves the camera movable; scene-camera playback adds its movement to your own framing. The speed slider changes preview speed without changing the MP4.
Save scene preserves custom settings, procedural recipes and the complete film sequence. Record MP4 from the initial state; the ending signature appears in the recorded video, not the live preview.
items.control_note: Select the Mobile preset in the current scene. An explicit MCP settings_preset applies immediately and resets paused; use settings_replay to run it. UI edits on a recent viewer remain pending until you choose Apply or Play.

items.label: Impact speed
items.hint: Initial push in metres per second. Increase speed before reducing brick mass.

items.label: Ball mass
items.hint: A heavier ball carries more momentum at the same speed.

items.label: Brick mass
items.hint: Heavier bricks resist the impact; lighter bricks scatter more easily.

items.label: Brick friction
items.hint: Higher friction reduces sliding after the impact.

items.label: Release angle
items.hint: Starting angle of the suspended ball, measured in degrees.

items.label: Wall rows
items.hint: Generate a shorter or taller wall without placing each brick manually.

items.label: Show chain
items.hint: Show or hide the link meshes; the suspension physics remains active.

items.label: Dust amount
items.hint: More visible dust without creating more physical bodies.

items.label: Cloud size
items.hint: Size of the individual dust puffs, in metres.

items.label: Cloud lifetime
items.hint: How long each puff remains visible.

items.label: Dust opacity
items.hint: Control transparency separately from cloud size and lifetime.

items.label: Minimum impact energy
items.hint: Only collisions above this energy emit dust. Lower it for gentler impacts.

items.label: Render quality
items.hint: Mobile uses lighter geometry and effects; Balanced is the everyday profile; Export uses full meshes.

items.label: Motion blur
items.hint: Rigid-object motion blur. It is disabled by the Mobile profile.

items.label: Brick edge radius
items.hint: Small bevels catch light along the edges. This remains bounded for the physics shape.

items.label: Brick colour variation
items.hint: Seeded colour variation shared by the procedural wall recipe.

experiments.title: 1. Gentle versus Demolition
experiments.text: Try Gentle (50 kg ball, 6 kg bricks, 2 m/s), then Demolition (100 kg ball, 0.75 kg bricks, 12 m/s). Apply and replay each preset; compare the opening and the debris.

experiments.title: 2. Make dust easier to see
experiments.text: Use Breach, then increase cloud size to 0.4 m and lifetime to 3 s. Change only one value at a time. On an updated viewer, lower the energy threshold for lighter impacts.

experiments.title: 3. Build for a phone
experiments.text: Choose Mobile: 18 rows, no motion blur and bounded dust. Check responsiveness on a real phone. Visual LOD does not change the physical colliders.

experiments.title: 4. Frame and record
experiments.text: Choose Cinematic for a desktop video. Preview with a free camera or at 0.5x, then record the authored sequence as MP4. Save the .scene alongside the video to keep the controls.

items.viewer_note: Live effects/body properties and queued initial-setup edits need the latest viewer. Earlier viewers either queue all edits or reset on release, and may omit dust opacity/energy threshold. Live grabbing, camera modes and speed controls also require a recent build.
items.title: Brick wall lab
items.description: Tune the impact, dust and render budget with 17 scene-owned controls.
items.prompt: Create a procedural brick wall and a wrecking ball on a physical chain. Add custom controls for impact, masses, wall height, dust and render quality, with Gentle, Breach, Demolition, Mobile and Cinematic presets.

items.title: Words in orbit
items.description: A real 3D ring of letters around a simple shape.
items.prompt: Create a cyan sphere and a golden 3D ring reading CREATE / VIEW / SHARE around it. Anchor the ring in world space, rotate it slowly and orbit the camera.

steps: Create three objects and compare their silhouettes.
Ask: Make the sphere larger and change the cube to purple.
Use Save scene to download a .scene file. Reopen it later to keep editing.
items.title: Your first three shapes
items.description: Create, recolour and resize three simple objects.
items.prompt: Create a cyan cube, a pink sphere and a golden cone side by side. Let them appear with blue edges and slowly orbit the camera.

steps: Create the objects with dynamic physics.
Start the simulation and listen to the impacts.
Pause to inspect a collision, then resume. Reset returns to the starting poses.
items.title: Let gravity do the work
items.description: Watch blocks and balls fall, bounce and settle.
items.prompt: Create a small stack of colourful blocks and balls above the ground. Let them fall with realistic collisions and subtle impact sounds.

steps: Frame the subject close without cutting it off.
Pull back, then blend smoothly into the orbit.
Ask: Show it from the other side, keeping the motion smooth.
items.title: A closer look
items.description: Move from a close detail to a smooth wider orbit.
items.prompt: Create a small colourful sculpture. Start the camera close, slowly pull back to reveal it and blend into a gentle orbit.

steps: The command field is an illustrative film overlay; it does not contact an AI.
Typing and validation sounds come from command-input-v2.
The scene change is authored in the same timeline, after validation.
items.control_note: This snippet adds the illustrative command field only. The blue colour change is a separate action in the downloadable scene.
items.title: A command comes to life
items.description: Animated typing, quiet cues and a glowing confirmation.
items.prompt: Show an animated command field typing “Make it blue”, then validate it softly and turn the sculpture blue. Use command-input-v2.

steps: Exports install the required signature automatically; creation prompts do not need to mention it.
For a custom ending, stop the film and install polynite-ending-v4.
Choose default or short-portrait placement and adjust volume. The fade, shine-only bloom and quiet cues stay together.
The signature remains required at export; paid removal is not enabled.
items.title: Make the ending yours
items.description: Keep the Polynite signature, choose its placement and soften its sound.
items.prompt: Use polynite-ending-v4 for this film. Put the closing signature higher with the short-portrait layout and lower its sound volume to 0.5.

steps: Prepare a film with the scene and camera moves. Save a .scene copy if you want to edit it later.
Record from the beginning; do not pre-play the film. Choose landscape or portrait and 30 or 60 FPS.
After recording, open Gallery > Videos. Preview with sound, then download the MP4 or use Open folder on desktop.
A .scene stays editable. An MP4 is the rendered movie. A Mint Link opens the interactive creation.
Download cloud videos you want to keep: uploaded MCP videos have seven-day retention.
items.title: From scene to MP4
items.description: Record a smooth film, preview it and keep your own copy.
items.prompt: Record this scene from the beginning as a landscape MP4 at 1080p and 60 FPS. Keep the sounds subtle, then show me where to download the video.

steps: Keep the tree trunks and canopies static, with colliders.
Use dynamic bodies only for the falling shapes.
Test a small rain first, then increase the count.
Frame the whole forest so the collisions remain easy to follow.
items.title: A forest under colourful rain
items.description: Static tree colliders meet falling spheres and cubes.
items.prompt: Create a small stylised forest with solid trunks and canopies. Drop colourful spheres and cubes onto it, with collisions, subtle sounds and a slow camera orbit.

steps: Use thin upright blocks and leave enough space for one to touch the next as it falls.
Give only the first block an initial tilt and angular velocity.
Use Reset scene to replay from the authored poses.
Change the spacing or friction and compare how far the chain travels.
items.title: One push, a chain reaction
items.description: A small impulse sends a row of coloured dominos tumbling.
items.prompt: Create a row of colourful dominos. Give the first one a gentle push and let the chain reaction unfold. Keep the camera close enough to see every collision.
